newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Houses said damaged after Indonesian earthquake.
newsitem.headline: Houses said damaged after Indonesian earthquake.

text.p: Hundreds of houses and schools in West Java were damaged or destroyed by Monday's earthquake, which also shook Indonesia's capital of Jakarta, the official Antara news agency reported on Wednesday.

Antara said houses and schools in some areas of south Banten in Pandeglang regency were affected by the earthquake, which measured 6.0 on the Richter scale. The epicentre was below the sea bed in the Indian ocean, about 300 km (200 miles) southwest of Jakarta.
There were no reports of casualties in Pandeglang, about 80 km (50 miles) west of Jakarta, but Antara said some areas remained cut off because of rugged terrain and lack of telephone lines.
Monday's earthquake was felt throughout West Java as well as in Lampung province on Sumatra and in Palembang, the capital of South Sumatra province.
In Jakarta, tall buildings shook and people rushed out onto the street. There were no reports of casualties, but some buildings were said to have developed cracks.
Meanwhile, Kompas newspaper said guidelines were to be issued on how to deal with earthquakes following the panic in Jakarta caused by Monday's tremor.
The Indonesian archipelago is on the edge of the geologically unstable zone circling the Pacific basin and known as the "ring of fire", and is earthquake prone.
